public_rationale: Lambda's October 1 financing is meaningful counterevidence: a sub-8% stated rate was attainable after publication. But the claim allows difficulty rather than absolute impossibility. One financing backed by strong customer contracts does not settle general access, and the disclosed rate is not a complete effective-cost calculation. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule.
limitations: Treating the wording as an absolute prohibition would produce a different assessment.
GPU financing and construction financing can have materially different risks.
Completed deals alone omit unsuccessful financing attempts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It will be difficult to impossible to raise AI data center debt at rates below 8%.

statement.excerpt: In simple terms, it’s going to be difficult to impossible to raise AI data center debt below 8%

our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts that new AI data center borrowing below 8% will generally become difficult to obtain.
Difficult to impossible allows some exceptions; it is not an unqualified claim that no sub-8% transaction can occur.
The nearby discussion of financing yields suggests effective annual borrowing cost, rather than coupon alone.
Building finance and GPU finance are relevant but must be distinguished. General-purpose corporate debt and convertible coupons are not automatically comparable.
No deadline is supplied. The evaluation date is an evidence cutoff, not an implied forecast deadline.
Estimate reflects the surrounding reliance on reported transaction pricing.
criteria.support_condition: Representative post-publication transactions and documented financing attempts show that sub-8% borrowing is generally difficult or unavailable. An indefinite forecast cannot receive conclusive support merely from a short period of expensive deals.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative post-publication financings establish that borrowers can routinely obtain comparable AI data center debt below 8% on ordinary commercial terms.

evidence.explanation: Lambda announced a closed, oversubscribed GPU-infrastructure facility backed by two investment-grade customers. This is material counterevidence to literal impossibility, but its stated interest rate and particular structure do not establish routine sector-wide access at an effective cost below 8%.

evidence.excerpt: Upfront fees, OID and undrawn fees are not added.
evidence.explanation: The financing inventory explicitly omits fees and original-issue discounts. Its displayed rates therefore cannot automatically be treated as complete effective borrowing costs.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative set of completed post-publication deals and financing attempts, including effective costs and terms, demonstrating whether sub-8% access is routine. A stated deadline would permit a bounded assessment.
